## find households in ESR data
```{r}
# registrations appearing in ESR
#' Title
#'
#' @param data1 dataframe. registration data
#' @param data2 dataframe. ESR data
#'
#' @returns a dataframe
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{check_esr_registrations(data1 = df_clean, data2 = df_esr)}
check_esr_registrations <- function(data1 = df_clean, data2 = df_esr) {

  
  # 1. prepare lookup keys from data2
  # combine names and clean id and phone for matching
  data2_prepared <- data2 %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      full_name_clean = clean_string(paste(first_name, middle_name, last_name)),
      first_surname = clean_string(paste(first_name, last_name)),
      first_secname = clean_string(paste(first_name, middle_name)),
      id_clean        = clean_string(id_number1),
      phone_clean     = clean_string(phone_number)
    )
  
  lookup_ids    <- unique(data2_prepared$id_clean)
  lookup_names  <- unique(data2_prepared$full_name_clean)
  lookup_names1  <- unique(data2_prepared$first_surname)
  lookup_names2  <- unique(data2_prepared$first_secname)
  lookup_phones <- unique(data2_prepared$phone_clean)
  
  # 2. apply matching logic to data1
  data1 %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      is_in_second_dataset = case_when(
        # check by id number
        clean_string(ben_id_number) %in% lookup_ids ~ "yes",
        
        # check by phone number using reg_num_phone
        clean_string(reg_num_phone) %in% lookup_phones ~ "yes",
        
        # check by combined name
        clean_string(ben_name) %in% lookup_names ~ "yes",
        clean_string(ben_first_surname) %in% lookup_names1 ~ "yes",
        clean_string(ben_first_secname) %in% lookup_names2 ~ "yes",
        
        # default to no if no matches are found
        TRUE ~ "no"
      )
    )
}
```

## export a list to excel
```{r}
#' export a named list of data frames to an excel workbook
#' @param df_list a named list of data frames
#' @param file_path character string for the output path
#' @returns NULL
#' @export
#' @examples
#' \dontrun{write_list_to_excel()}
write_list_to_excel <- function(df_list, file_path) {
  
  # create a new workbook object
  wb <- openxlsx::createWorkbook()
  
  # define a professional header style
  header_style <- createStyle(
    fgFill = "#4F81BD", 
    halign = "center", 
    textDecoration = "bold",
    fontColour = "white",
    border = "bottom"
  )
  
  # iterate through the named list
  # .x is the dataframe, .y is the name of the list element
  purrr::iwalk(df_list, function(.x, .y) {
    
    # add a new worksheet with the name of the list element
    # excel sheet names are limited to 31 characters
    sheet_name <- substr(.y, 1, 31)
    openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, sheet_name)
    
    # write the data to the sheet
    openxlsx::writeData(wb, sheet_name, .x, headerStyle = header_style)
    
    # adjust column widths to fit content automatically
    openxlsx::setColWidths(wb, sheet_name, cols = 1:ncol(.x), widths = "auto")
    
    # freeze the top row for easier navigation
    openxlsx::freezePane(wb, sheet_name, firstRow = TRUE)
  })
  
  # save the workbook to the specified path
  openxlsx::saveWorkbook(wb, file_path, overwrite = TRUE)
}
```
